title: History-taking & Communication
sourceNote: Items follow the school communication checklist, paraphrased in our own words. Items needing body language are marked not_assessable pending team confirmation (see docs/PLAN.md).

items.label: Greets the patient by name
items.guidance: Student greets the patient and uses the patient’s name (any form, e.g. Mr./Ms. + surname or first name if invited).

items.label: Removes barriers to communication (sits down, breaks computer contact)
items.notAssessableReason: Body position and screen use are not visible in this interface (possible with VR later).

items.label: Checks comfort, readiness and privacy; puts patient at ease
items.guidance: Student asks whether the patient is comfortable / ready, or addresses privacy, or makes a remark that puts the patient at ease.

items.label: Elicits chief concern with an open-ended question
items.guidance: An open question to elicit the main concern (e.g. What brings you in today?). Closed questions do not count.
mockKeywords: what can i do for you

items.label: Elicits additional concerns with an open-ended question
items.guidance: Asks whether there is anything else the patient wants to address today, before diving into the HPI.

items.label: Notes additional issues to discuss today
items.guidance: Acknowledges/lists the additional issues raised so they are not lost (e.g. We will also talk about X).

items.label: Prioritises concerns if necessary
items.guidance: If more than one concern exists, negotiates which to focus on first. If the patient raised only one concern, score 1 only if the student explicitly confirmed there was nothing else to prioritise; otherwise 0.

items.label: Invites the patient’s story with an open-ended prompt
items.guidance: Invites the patient’s narrative with an open prompt (e.g. Tell me about…).

items.label: Uses non-verbal / paraverbal encouragement (nodding, silence)
items.notAssessableReason: Nodding and silence are not captured in a text transcript (possible with voice/VR later).

items.label: Uses a second or third open question / echoing to get more story
items.guidance: After the first answer, uses another open prompt or echoes the patient’s words to invite more.

items.label: Clarifies by summarising
items.guidance: Summarises or checks understanding (e.g. Let me make sure I have this right…).

items.label: Elicits emotional context
items.guidance: Asks how the problem is affecting the patient emotionally / how they are coping.

items.label: Elicits personal context
items.guidance: Asks what the problem means for the patient’s life (work, family, activities, roles).

items.label: Responds to emotional or personal context (empathy)
items.guidance: Explicitly acknowledges or validates the patient’s feelings or situation.

items.label: Clarifies the timeline
items.guidance: Establishes when it started and how it evolved over time.

items.label: Onset
items.guidance: Asks how the symptom began (sudden vs gradual, what they were doing).

items.label: Duration
items.guidance: Asks how long the symptom has been present / how long episodes last.

items.label: Quality
items.guidance: Asks what the symptom feels like.

items.label: Quantification / severity
items.guidance: Quantifies severity or functional impact (scale, distance walked, number of pillows, etc.).

items.label: Related symptoms
items.guidance: Asks about associated symptoms.

items.label: Setting
items.guidance: Asks the setting in which it occurs (exertion, lying flat, time of day, at night).

items.label: Transforming factors
items.guidance: Asks what makes it better or worse.

items.label: Uses closed questions to narrow the differential
items.guidance: Asks specific yes/no questions aimed at raising or lowering particular diagnoses (e.g. chest pain, fever, leg pain, medication adherence).

items.label: Summarises the HPI and checks accuracy
items.guidance: Gives a summary of the HPI back to the patient and asks if it is accurate.

items.label: Signposts the move to more directed questions
items.guidance: Tells the patient they will now ask about past history / other questions.

items.label: PMH: conditions
items.guidance: Asks about past medical conditions.

items.label: PMH: when diagnosed
items.guidance: Asks when conditions were diagnosed.

items.label: PSH: surgeries / procedures
items.guidance: Asks about past surgeries or procedures.

items.label: PSH: dates
items.guidance: Asks when surgeries/procedures happened.

items.label: Medications: names
items.guidance: Asks what medications the patient takes.

items.label: Medications: doses
items.guidance: Asks about doses / how often taken.

items.label: Medications: over-the-counter and supplements
items.guidance: Asks specifically about OTC medicines, herbal products or supplements.

items.label: Allergies: drug
items.guidance: Asks about medication allergies.

items.label: Allergies: food
items.guidance: Asks about food allergies.

items.label: Allergies: type of reaction
items.guidance: Asks what reaction occurred.

items.label: FH: parents and siblings living / age and cause of death
items.guidance: Asks about the health of parents and siblings, and age/cause of death where applicable.

items.label: SH: alcohol
items.guidance: Asks about alcohol. For items marked "if relevant": score 1 if asked OR if clearly not relevant to this case and reasonably omitted; score 0 only if relevant and omitted.

items.label: SH: smoking / tobacco
items.guidance: Asks about smoking / tobacco. For items marked "if relevant": score 1 if asked OR if clearly not relevant to this case and reasonably omitted; score 0 only if relevant and omitted.

items.guidance: Asks about travel (if relevant). For items marked "if relevant": score 1 if asked OR if clearly not relevant to this case and reasonably omitted; score 0 only if relevant and omitted.

items.guidance: Asks at least one screening question for the General system (either during the HPI or in a review of systems).

items.label: Transitions to the physical exam
items.guidance: Tells the patient they will now examine them and asks permission.

items.label: Shares assessment in plain language
items.guidance: Explains what they think is going on in language a patient understands (no unexplained jargon).
mockKeywords: what i think is going on

items.label: Explains the plan or choices in plain language
items.guidance: Describes next steps (tests, treatment, admission) in plain language.

items.label: Elicits questions, concerns and preferences
items.guidance: Asks what the patient thinks / prefers, or what concerns they have about the plan.

items.label: Confirms agreement and understanding (teach-back)
items.guidance: Checks understanding, ideally by asking the patient to repeat back the plan.

items.label: Checks for any other questions before ending
Reviews expectancies and safety-netting
items.guidance: Tells the patient what will happen next and what should prompt them to call/return.
